assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology to GLP-1 receptor agonists is a rare complete arc from hormone discovery to therapies with large effects on diabetes, obesity and cardiometabolic outcomes. Impact is already enormous and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: Credit is genuinely contested: Mojsov (peptide chemistry, active GLP-1(7-36) form), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, therapeutic rationale), Holst (physiology and incretin effect) and Knudsen (liraglutide/semaglutide drug development) all made decisive contributions. Three names is a tight fit; basic-science trio proposed, with Habener-type contributions not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independent confirmation across multiple drug classes and large outcome trials; timing is arguably overdue given global clinical impact.
uncertainties: Four credited names exceed the three-laureate cap, so Knudsen's industrial drug-development role is left out.
Allocation among Mojsov, Drucker and Holst and relative to uncredited early contributors is unresolved (my knowledge, not verified here).
Long-term safety and durability data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience a general method for causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with light, reshaping circuit physiology and enabling work across systems. Originality and breadth of lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins; Boyden and Deisseroth (with Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photostimulation) established neuronal use. Six credited names; I propose Nagel for the channelrhodopsin discovery plus Deisseroth and Boyden for neuronal implementation, but Hegemann, Bamberg and Miesenböck have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and ubiquitous for over fifteen years; clearly mature and timely, with clinical use in vision restoration emerging.
uncertainties: Genuinely difficult three-person allocation among six credited people.
Whether the tool or the underlying microbial opsin discovery is the prize-worthy unit is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living drugs; discovery-to-patient impact is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CD28 costimulated CARs), June (4-1BB CAR and first clinical successes in leukemia) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials) form a plausible trio. Earlier CAR concept contributions from others (e.g. Eshhar, Gross) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products with years of follow-up; mature. Limits in solid tumors and toxicity remain but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric-receptor concept is outside the supplied names.
Rosenberg's contribution is adjacent (TIL, adoptive transfer) rather than CAR-specific.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-term culture of Lgr5+ adult stem cells as self-organizing organoids created a widely used platform for tissue biology, disease modeling and personalized-medicine research. Conceptually clear and broadly adopted.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell identification and organoid culture, with Sato as first author of the foundational intestinal organoid work. A clean two-person configuration within the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and extended in numerous organs and labs for over a decade; mature in research use, while clinical translation is still early.
uncertainties: Relation to broader stem-cell and 3D-culture precedents may complicate originality arguments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided antisense correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) converted spinal muscular atrophy from a fatal childhood disease into a treatable one, validating splice-switching oligonucleotides as a therapeutic modality.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and ASO target, Bennett led oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development; the supplied two names map well to the decisive contributions.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong long-term clinical evidence; the modality is established and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Contributions of other groups (e.g. Singh/Singh, Hua) to SMN2 splicing targets are not in the supplied credit.
Modality-level versus single-drug framing is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed to trigger innate immunity, with implications for infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunology. Clear, original mechanistic pathway with wide impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger; Barber identified STING. Supplied credit includes others on the cGAS work (Sun, Wu) and Ishikawa on STING; a Chen and Barber pairing is the cleanest within the exact names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed independently and extensively; therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) has not yet delivered approved drugs, so clinical validation is premature.
uncertainties: Allocation to co-first authors versus lab heads is debatable.
Therapeutic payoff is not yet shown.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as a survival rather than proliferation oncogene redefined cancer biology, established the apoptosis regulatory network, and led to BH3 mimetics such as venetoclax in clinical use.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterized the translocated BCL-2 gene and its biology; Vaux demonstrated its anti-apoptotic function in vivo; Strasser's work on BH3-only/Bim and pathway logic is also important. Four credited names exceed the cap; Strasser is left out, and Vaux versus Strasser is unresolved. Original BCL-2 cloning by Tsujimoto/Croce is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed, with an approved drug class; mature and timely, though apoptosis already has a prior Nobel (2002), which may weigh on novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 Nobel prize on programmed cell death.
Fair allocation across four credited people is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL11A as a repressor of fetal hemoglobin explained fetal-to-adult switching and enabled BCL11A enhancer editing therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia, a strong human-genetics-to-therapy story.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran identified and functionally established BCL11A; Bauer showed enhancer dependence and editing strategy; Thein contributed GWAS-linked HbF genetics. Orkin and Sankaran are proposed; Bauer's editing contribution is a close alternative.
assessment.maturity: Therapy approved recently (2023), so clinical follow-up is still short; science is well confirmed but recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Long-term safety and access for the gene-editing therapy are unproven.
Relative weight of the genetic-association and editing contributions is unresolved.
